draft.title: The origins of Buddhism
card: Buddhism began in northern India about 2,500 years ago. It grew from the teachings of one man, Siddhartha Gautama.
Siddhartha was born into a ruling family of a small kingdom. Tradition says he left his comfortable home to search for an answer to why people suffer.
After years of searching, he is said to have gained awakening, a deep understanding of the true nature of life. From then on he was called the Buddha, which means the awakened one.
The Buddha then spent decades teaching others what he had understood. His followers kept these teachings, and they became the religion called Buddhism.
draft.remember: Buddhism began with Siddhartha Gautama, who became the Buddha after he gained awakening.

a.q: What does the title Buddha mean?
opts: The one who gave up wealth
a.why: Buddha means the awakened one, a title Siddhartha Gautama received after he gained awakening. Giving up wealth was part of his search, but it is not what the title means.
a.clue: The title describes what Siddhartha gained after his search.

b.q: Mei reads that a man in northern India left his home to search for answers and later began teaching. Which person is this?
opts: Siddhartha Gautama, who became the Buddha
A Buddhist follower who copied the teachings
A king who ruled a small kingdom in India
A teacher who began Buddhism 500 years ago
b.why: Siddhartha Gautama left home, gained awakening and then taught, so Buddhism grew from him. A later follower kept the teachings but did not begin them.
b.clue: Think about who the religion grew from.

b.best: Siddhartha Gautama, who became the Buddha
